title: Integral torus Euler characters and canonical geometric realization predicates
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Use the existing group-scheme characters $X=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$, written additively, and $R=\mathbf Z[X]$ [def-sfb-trivial-torus-coherent-data]. For an affine group scheme $T$ and a finite-dimensional rational coordinate comodule $(V,c)$ [def-sfb-rational-representation-gzero], put $V_\chi=\{v:c(v)=v\otimes\chi\}$, with $\chi$ evaluated on the universal point, and define $\operatorname{ch}_T(V)=\sum_\chi(\dim_F V_\chi)e^\chi$ and $D_T(V)=\prod_\chi(1-e^\chi)^{\dim_F V_\chi}$. These are the finite-support sum and product (totalized by zero and one, respectively, outside finite support); weight decomposition will establish finite support for a split torus. Put $\Sigma=\langle1-e^\chi:\chi\ne0\rangle$ and $R_\Sigma=\Sigma^{-1}R$. Restriction of a rational $H$-module to a closed subgroup $T\hookrightarrow H$ [def-sfb-equivariant-coherent-groups] is characterized, up to linear comodule isomorphism, by applying $F[H]\to F[T]$ to every coefficient of its coaction. For an equivariant coherent sheaf $E$ on an $H$-scheme, a realization of its rational cohomology in degree $q$ is a rational module associated to a coherent sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}F$ whose underlying sheaf is $R^qf_*E$ for the structure map and whose linearization is the all-degree base-change linearization [lem-sfb-equivariant-coherent-proper-pushforward]; record also its vector-space identification with the existing Zariski cohomology. For an equivariant coherent $E$ on a $T$-scheme $Z$ and a fixed rational point $p$, a fibre pair consists of rational modules associated to the equivariant pullbacks of $E$ and of the ideal of $p$, respectively, using the existing normalized operation predicates [def-sfb-equivariant-coherent-gzero]. The latter pullback is $\mathfrak m_p/\mathfrak m_p^2$, with the dual derivative action. These are explicit definitions and predicates, with no existence assertion or choice of a representation.

source.place: Section 22d, proof of Theorem 22.50, p.480: general fixed-point input, stated here in its integral equivariant form; Example 22.36, pp.473--474, for formal characters.
